ovaries.def: The paired female gonads, almond-sized organs against the pelvic side walls. Their cortex holds ovarian follicles (each an oocyte wrapped in supporting cells) and they make estrogen and progesterone; the ovarian ligament ties each to the uterus and the suspensory ligament, which carries its vessels, ties it to the pelvic wall.

uterine-tubes.def: Two muscular tubes, about 10 cm long, from the uterus toward the ovaries (also called fallopian tubes or oviducts). Each has an open end fringed with fimbriae, a wide ampulla where sperm usually meet the oocyte, and a narrow isthmus next to the uterus; cilia and smooth muscle move the oocyte toward the uterus.

uterus.def: The hollow, pear-shaped muscular organ in which an embryo develops, with a fundus, body and cervix, draped by the broad ligament. Its wall has an outer perimetrium, a thick smooth muscle myometrium and an inner endometrium, whose functional layer is shed at menstruation and regrown from the basal layer.

vagina-vulva.def: The vagina is a gland-free, acidic muscular tube, 7 to 10 cm long, from the vaginal opening to the cervix, with a hymen at its opening. The vulva is the external genitals: the mons pubis, labia majora and minora, the clitoris, the vestibule and the greater vestibular (Bartholin's) glands.

mammary-glands.def: Exocrine glands in the breast that can make milk. Milk-making alveoli, grouped into lobules and lobes, drain through branching ducts into lactiferous ducts that open at the nipple, with a slight widening near the nipple called the lactiferous sinus; the pigmented areola surrounds the nipple.
